title: Quant CI harness: golden calibration sets, deterministic digests, and rotation playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Build a CI/QA harness and operational playbook to guarantee reproducible quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8) across calibration runs, enable secure digest signing and digest rotation, and provide a deterministic rollback path for serving. This ticket consolidates tasks for datasets (golden calibration sets), RNG and compiler seeding, digesting strategy, CI checks, and the operator-facing rotation/rollback playbook.

Context: Current quant artifact generation shows subtle nondeterminism across runs (heap layout, non-seeded ops, CPU/GPU kernel variance) that causes different hashes for functionally equivalent artifacts. This complicates rollbacks and auditability for customers using Dedicated/Private. We need a pragmatic, cross-team approach that balances engineering cost and regulatory traceability while preserving throughput for production re-quantizations and model onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: A CI pipeline job that reproducibly computes a stable artifact digest for quant artifacts given an explicit seed and calibration snapshot
Canonical golden calibration datasets checked into immutable storage with versioned references (URI + dataset-digest) used by CI
A documented digest format and signing scheme (digest algorithm, metadata fields included, and attestation step) stored alongside artifacts
Digest rotation playbook: steps to rotate keys, re-sign artifacts, and notify downstream consumers without breaking inference routing

Validation harness compares accuracy/metric deltas against baseline using the golden eval set and flags regressions beyond configured thresholds (e.g., top-1 token KL, EM, and percent accuracy depending on workload)
tasks: Design digest schema: fields to include (model-id, model-version, quant-profile-id, calibration-dataset-id+digest, seed, compiler-flags, toolchain-version, timestamp, builder-pr)
Create a deterministic build wrapper that records RNG state and calls quant toolchains with fixed environment variables and pinned kernels
Curate and finalize golden calibration + evaluation sets (small representative slices for quick CI + full sets for nightly re-checks). Store as immutable objects (GCS/S3) with content-addressed keys
Add CI job that: fetches golden set -> runs calibration with provided seed and flags -> produces quant artifact -> computes canonical digest -> runs evaluation harness -> compares metrics to baseline
Implement signing step (GPG/PKI) for digests and store signed manifests in artifacts bucket along with human-readable attestations
Document operator playbook for digest rotation and rollback: hotfix flow, emergency rollback, and compatibility checks for older serving binaries
Add dashboard alerts for digest mismatches and accuracy regressions; link to PR, pipeline run, and evaluation artifact URLs
notes:
Implementation notes: For FP8-specific variability, include per-layer stochastic summaries (e.g., scaling distribution histograms) in the artifact metadata to make nondeterministic differences visible. For INT8, ensure calibration collect mode uses deterministic ordering of data batches and explicit accumulation precision. Use a single canonical digest algorithm (SHA-256) and define canonical serialization (sorted JSON keys, UTF-8) to avoid incidental changes.

Operational constraints: Signed manifests must be backward compatible with existing release tooling used by Dedicated customers. Key rotation should support an overlap window where both old and new signatures are accepted for reads to avoid blocking serving during a rotation.

Open questions: How much of the runtime kernel determinism must be solved vs. documented as 'known variability' with tolerance thresholds? Do we require attestation-level signing for all internal quick-turn artifacts or only release candidates?
acceptance_test_instructions: Run the CI job locally via ./ci/run_quant_repro.sh --seed 42 --cal-dataset-uri gs://redwood-quant/golden-sets/mini/sha256:<digest> and confirm: produced artifact digest matches reference, signed manifest exists, and evaluation metrics fall within thresholds defined in /ci/baselines/<model>-baseline.json
operational_playbook_summary: 1) Verify signed manifest and digest. 2) If digest mismatch but metrics OK, tag artifact as 'equivalent' and create signed equivalence attestation. 3) For metric regressions > threshold, block rollout and open PR to re-calibrate with increased sample size. 4) For key rotation: publish new public key to trust store, sign manifests under both keys for 72-hour overlap, then revoke old key. 5) Rollback flow: download previous signed artifact, run smoke eval with golden set, re-register artifact in model catalog and trigger canary rollout
implementation_team_notes: Coordinate with Serving Runtime (kernel selection) and Build Infra to pin toolchain versions. Notify Security for signing key custody. Plan for a nightlies lane that runs full-eval (larger datasets) and a PR lane for quick sanity checks.
customer_communication_snippet: We are introducing reproducible quant artifacts and signed manifests so customers can confidently pin a quantized model version and roll back deterministically. This improves auditability for Dedicated and Private deployments.
